neighbours.label: the piece 'inct' in the word 'tincture' (t|inct|ure); not 'inct' in distinct/extinct/precinct
fire: The herbalist sold a small bottle of valerian tincture for sleep.
In heraldry the tinctures are divided into metals, colours and furs.
Old pharmacies kept tincture of opium on a locked shelf.
He rubbed a little arnica tincture into the bruise.
The recipe says to dilute the tincture with warm water before drinking.
Alcohol is the usual solvent when making a tincture from dried roots.
The arms are described with the tincture of the field first.
A few drops of propolis tincture were added to the honey.
quiet: The herbalist sold a small bottle of valerian syrup for sleep.
In heraldry the colours are divided into metals, enamels and furs.
Old pharmacies kept bottles of opium on a locked shelf.
He rubbed a little arnica cream into the bruise.
The two dialects are distinct enough to confuse visitors.
The species went extinct soon after the forest was cleared.
Voters in the third precinct waited an hour in the rain.
A few drops of propolis extract were added to the honey.

notes: Card: 'inct' x6 after ' t' (tincture), also ' tarn', 'ully'. Probes: tincture 0.96-1.15, extract 0.01, distinct/extinct/precinct/succinct <= 0.02, tarn 0.56 (not tested here).
